experience:
Kontur — Frontend developer
May 2024 — present
Kontur.Logistics — a service for electronic exchange of transport documents. About 100 people in 4 sub-teams, several SPA applications in a monorepo, Scrum. My sub-team develops shared modules and mechanisms for the other sub-teams.
- As a feature lead, moved every screen of the application for 6 user roles to the new design. The release shipped on time, users rated the new interface 4.3 out of 5. Led a feature team of two frontend developers, two designers and a QA engineer; planned the release and agreed the rollout plan with support and experts — no critical incidents and no spike in support requests.
- Reworked the application shell: split the overgrown layout into three, and the single menu with a shared config into separate components for each role. Now changes for one role don't affect the others.
- Designed a shared frontend metrics mechanism with a single entry point: the product collects 300+ metrics through it. Together with analysts, set up a process where metrics are planned before development. I own this area: support, development, consulting the teams.
- As a feature lead, moved 12 step-by-step onboarding tours, seen by ~15 thousand users a month, to Kontur's shared solution in 2 weeks. Now tours are created without developers: more than five new ones have already appeared.
- Developed shared modules for the Logistics applications: non-blocking file upload with a background mode and a single banner manager with logic separated from markup.
- Designed and developed a responsive interface for a new role in a month. The feature shipped on time.
- Cover features with unit and screenshot tests, review code of neighbouring sub-teams, help onboard new frontend developers.
